title: College Panda Ch 6 Ex 2: Lines & Linear Relationships

questions.stem: The graph of the linear function $f$ is shown in the $xy$-plane. What is the slope of the graph of $f$?

figures.alt: Line through (0, 2) and (4, 0), grid from −2 to 6 on x and −2 to 4 on y.

questions.stem: Line $j$ is defined by $4x+20y=5$. Line $k$ is parallel to line $j$ in the $xy$-plane. What is the slope of line $k$?

The linear function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=ax+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants. If the graph of $y=f(x)$ in the $xy$-plane has a slope of $6$ and passes through the point $(-5,-14)$, what is the value of $b$?
What is the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept of the graph of $7x=6\left(15+\dfrac{9x}{4}-\dfrac{4y}{7}\right)$ in the $xy$-plane?
The graph of the equation $ax+by=-4$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants, is shown in the $xy$-plane. What is the value of $ab$?

figures.alt: Line through (−4, 0) and (0, 1), grid from −5 to 4 on x and −2 to 3 on y.

questions.stem: A line in the $xy$-plane is defined by the equation $y=ax+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants. The line passes through the points $(0,-79)$ and $(5,91)$. What is the value of $a+b$?
In the $xy$-plane, the line with equation $ax-\frac{1}{3}y=8$, where $a$ is a constant, passes through the point $(2,6)$. What is the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept of the line?

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline x & y\\ \hline -6 & -114-p\\ \hline -2 & -57-p\\ \hline 2 & -p\\ \hline\end{array}$$

The table shows three values of $x$ and their corresponding values of $y$, where $p$ is a constant. There is a linear relationship between $x$ and $y$. What is the slope of the line that represents this relationship in the $xy$-plane?

The graph of the equation $5x-8y=k$, where $k$ is a constant, is a line in the $xy$-plane. The line has an $x$-intercept at $(m,0)$ and a $y$-intercept at $(0,n)$, where $m$ and $n$ are constants. What is the value of $\dfrac{m}{n}$?

In the $xy$-plane, the graph of the linear function $f$ has a negative slope and a $y$-intercept at $(0,k)$, where $k$ is a positive constant. Which of the following must be true?
I. If $a>b$, then $f(a)II. If $a<0$, then $f(a)>k$.
III. If $a>0$, then $f(a)>0$.
In the $xy$-plane, the points $(-3,5)$ and $(6,8)$ lie on line $l$. Which of the following points also lies on line $l$?

$$y=\frac{a}{b}x+c$$ $$y=\frac{d}{e}x+c$$ In the given pair of equations, $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, and $e$ are constants. The pair of equations represent two perpendicular lines in the $xy$-plane. If $0<\dfrac{a}{b}<1$, which of the following must be true?

In the $xy$-plane, line $p$ passes through the point $(1,n)$, where $n$ is a constant. Line $q$ intersects line $p$ at the point $(0,0)$ and is perpendicular to line $p$. Which of the following points must lie on line $q$?
In the $xy$-plane, line $m$ has an $x$-intercept at $(a,b+4)$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants. If line $m$ passes through the points $(b,-11)$ and $(b+6,7)$, what is the value of $a$?
The function $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\dfrac{f(x)+6}{x}$, where $f$ is a linear function. The partial graph of $y=g(x)$ is shown. What is the $y$-intercept of the graph of $y=f(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?

questions.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the line with equation $ax-by=5$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants, is perpendicular to the line with equation $11x-4y=5$. Which of the following equations represents a line that is perpendicular to the line with equation $11x+12y=5$?
